transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start: 09:30 PT
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Meeting recorded by Fireflies

Summary:
Quick primer on fallback tiers (what we call corridor / shipping corridor), triage of outstanding stability items for the upcoming slate, and firming next steps for canary and rollforward. Heavy discussion on KV cache edge-cases and SLO tradeoffs.

Topics:
- Fallback tiers and policy mapping
- Shipping corridor traffic shaping and canary matrix
- KV cache bypass patterns for low-latency small seqs
- RBAC/audit gating for private builds
- Chaos test plan and schedule

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: okay everyone, thanks for jumping on on short notice. i've put an agenda in the doc, link in chat, but high level — fallback primer, shipping corridor triage, then we map owners.
[00:00:12] Samir Patel: yep, thanks. i'm going to start with a quick sketch of current runtime behavior when we drop into fallback 2 vs 3, because i think some of the confusion stems from how kv cache and batching interact.
[00:00:25] Tom Hargreaves: can we also call out the dedicated vs hosted differences? i feel like some of the rollout notes assume hosted-only semantics.
[00:00:31] Maya Chen: good call, tom. we'll flag them.
[00:00:34] Jules Park: i'll note that our telemetry for cache-miss latency is kinda noisy in staging, so numbers may be +/- 10 to 20 percent, not precise.
[00:00:45] Lina Gomez: quick q, when you say fallback 2, do you mean the model variant fallback or the region fallback? we've seen folks conflate the two.
[00:00:52] Samir Patel: model variant mainly, but the policy can chain into region fallback if latency SLOs breach across the pool. it's a cascade. bad naming on us maybe.
[00:01:05] Rajiv Menon: i put a note in the sheet about replication lag spikes when we flip model variants — those correlate with large KV cache invalidations.
[00:01:14] Maya Chen: ok, let's walk the canary matrix. Slide 2 in the doc — we have corridor lanes 0-3, where 0 is dry-run, 1 is low-traffic canary, 2 is partial ramp, 3 is full rollforward. we want to verify thresholds for 1 and 2.
[00:01:29] Samir Patel: current thresholds: latency P95 < 250ms, error increase < +0.5%, token cost delta < +15% else rollback. those numbers came from old experiments; we should revalidate against recent quantized kernels.
[00:01:44] Maya Chen: action: consolidate matrix and mark where these are opinionated.
[00:01:48] Elena Ruiz: link to sheet in chat — https://short.link/canary-matrix (uploaded)
[00:01:55] Tom Hargreaves: i want to call out one scenario: small-shot completions where sequence lengths are tiny — the batching and kv lookup overhead makes latency worse under our standard path. we may need a bypass.
[00:02:07] Samir Patel: yeah — i prototyped a 'kv-bypass' hop that avoids prefix cache for seq < 32 tokens. early numbers look promising but need more runs.
[00:02:18] Rajiv Menon: are you seeing accuracy regressions when bypassing kv? that's my main worry.
[00:02:22] Samir Patel: negligible for short responses, but for multi-turn it's dangerous because the model loses context. so we gate it to cases where we detect short single-turn prompts. imperfect detector tho.
[00:02:35] Maya Chen: note: that gating classifier needs to be conservative. safer to err on not bypassing if uncertain.
[00:02:41] Jules Park: from an ops perspective, bypass reduces tail latency but increases GPU cycles — we need to show cost delta to release team.
[00:02:49] Lina Gomez: i'll add that to infra checklist — cost delta must be under 8% for corridor 2 to be allowed.
[00:02:56] Maya Chen: good. next, RBAC and private builds — lina?
[00:03:01] Lina Gomez: we found one missing audit-log for VPC-key rotation last week. for private customers we must ensure KMS events are surfaced to the console. so RBAC gating: only infra-sig and release-engineering can flip corridor 3. we'll put that in the runbook.
[00:03:16] Tom Hargreaves: and add SSO requirement for any canary approvals — no email-based approvals for high-risk corridors.
[00:03:22] Maya Chen: agreed.
[00:03:25] [00:03:26] — short crosstalk, someone drops a can of coffee noise —
[00:03:30] Samir Patel: on chaos tests — jules, you had a script to simulate routing bucket exhaustion?
[00:03:35] Jules Park: yes. the plan: two runs. run A simulates zone failover with 10% extra latency, run B ramps request volume on corridor 1 to 40% and shifts weight off global pool. the script will also flip policy to fallback-variant X to ensure fall-through works.
[00:03:53] Rajiv Menon: can the chaos runner also validate tracing spans so we can see where KV invalidations show up end-to-end?
[00:03:58] Jules Park: yes, but tracing sampling needs to be increased for that window. requires a short retention bump.
[00:04:05] Maya Chen: what's the retention cost estimate?
[00:04:07] Jules Park: minimal for 1 hour window, maybe an extra 2GB. we'll put numbers in the ticket.
[00:04:12] Maya Chen: ok.
[00:04:15] [00:04:16] — 00:04:16 timestamp skip —
[00:04:20] Tom Hargreaves: one more runtime nuance — kernel fallback path sometimes reorders kernels leading to tiny correctness diffs in logits for long sequences, which can cascade to completions. QA flagged one example where the output wording changed enough to fail a downstream parser.
[00:04:36] Samir Patel: that's the quant-kernel skew we saw in the last canary. patch in the kernel selector to pin heuristics when sequence length > 512. but that reduces some perf headroom. tradeoff.
[00:04:48] Maya Chen: decision point: keep pinned selector for corridor 1/2 until post-launch data proves it's safe to un-pin.
[00:04:56] Lina Gomez: i second that. safer.
[00:04:59] Rajiv Menon: QA can add a regression prompt set that runs against canaries to detect parser failures early. i'll add initial 120 prompts.
[00:05:07] Samir Patel: cool. i'll expose a /health/regression endpoint we can hit as part of canary checks.
[00:05:13] Elena Ruiz: timeline check — are we trying to ship this slate in the week of 10/18?
[00:05:18] Maya Chen: target yes, but we need corridor 1 verification by 10/09 to be comfortable with that.
[00:05:24] Tom Hargreaves: also need legal sign-off for changes that affect data retention for private builds — Lina, can you loop them in?
[00:05:31] Lina Gomez: yeah, i'll cc legal on the runbook PR.
[00:05:34] [00:05:35] — brief pause while someone pulls up a doc —
[00:05:40] Maya Chen: let's go through the open defects table (sheet). i'll read them quickly and assign. first: 'staging telemetry gaps for kv cache'.
[00:05:49] Jules Park: that's mine. cause: sampling config was rolled back in staging; i missed the env flag. root fix is to add an integration test that asserts sampling is on.
[00:05:58] Maya Chen: jules, add the test and reference the ticket. due 10/09.
[00:06:03] Jules Park: noted.
[00:06:05] Maya Chen: next: 'canary rollback lacks automated remediation for model hotfix'.
[00:06:11] Samir Patel: this is a deeper workflow thing — we can automate a rollback hook that flips routing back to previous variant and flushes prefix cache for the old variant. but need to ensure no double-flush races.
[00:06:24] Rajiv Menon: also test for burst of errors on rollback window. we had one incident where rollback increased errors for 2 min.
[00:06:31] Maya Chen: we should script a canary rollback scenario in chaos and verify recovery.
[00:06:35] Samir Patel: ok, i'll prototype the hook and run it in staging with jules.
[00:06:39] Maya Chen: good.
[00:06:41] [00:06:42] Tom Hargreaves: question — are we comfortable with the cost vs benefit of keeping KV-bypass as an opt-in feature for hosted customers? some customers will enable it and then wonder about unpredictability.
[00:06:55] Lina Gomez: must be behind a feature flag and documented — include explicit SLO caveats. also require customer acceptance if it's a dedicated pool.
[00:07:05] Maya Chen: add docs item to the rollout checklist. elena?
[00:07:09] Elena Ruiz: i'll own documentation and the customer comms blurb. will draft by 10/07.
[00:07:15] Maya Chen: perfect.
[00:07:18] [00:07:19] — interruption, someone mentions lunch delivery —
[00:07:25] Samir Patel: back to kernels — can we get a tiny A/B in corridor 1 where 10% traffic uses the unpinned selector to collect telemetry without risk?
[00:07:36] Tom Hargreaves: maybe too risky for corridor 1; corridor 0 (dry run) is safer. but i like the idea of sampling.
[00:07:42] Maya Chen: we'll add a telemetry-only lane in corridor 0 for kernel selector experiments. no customer traffic should be affected.
[00:07:50] Rajiv Menon: QA will run the parser regression set against that telemetry lane and compare diffs.
[00:07:55] Maya Chen: sweet.
[00:07:58] [00:07:59] — 00:07:59 marker —
[00:08:02] Jules Park: scheduling: chaos runs are greenlighted for 10/09 in staging. jules will run with a 2 hour window starting 09:00.
[00:08:10] Jules Park: and i'll bump tracing sampling for the window.
[00:08:13] Lina Gomez: release watch: who will be oncall for the corridor 1 ramp if things go sideways?
[00:08:18] Tom Hargreaves: i'll cover the first ramp window 9-11 PT, rajiv takes the 11-1 slot.
[00:08:25] Rajiv Menon: yep.
[00:08:27] Maya Chen: put those in the sheet.
[00:08:29] Elena Ruiz: adding now.
[00:08:32] [00:08:33] — short pause —
[00:08:37] Maya Chen: any other risks?
[00:08:39] Samir Patel: one more — edge case: model routing can pick a smaller quantized variant that's not strictly architecture-compatible, resulting in weird return shapes in the streaming API. we've seen a mismatch where streaming tokens end early.
[00:08:53] Rajiv Menon: that explains the parser fail earlier.
[00:08:55] Samir Patel: patching the router to check compatibility signatures should fix it. i'll add that ticket.
[00:09:00] Maya Chen: add engineering priority P1 for router-compat check.
[00:09:03] Samir Patel: noted.
[00:09:05] [00:09:06] — later in call, time advance implied —
[00:35:12] Maya Chen: mid-call recap: assigned owners, canary matrix updated, chaos on 10/09, docs and legal looped, need corridor 1 verification by 10/09 to aim at ship week 10/18.
[00:35:23] Tom Hargreaves: also agreed to conservative kernel selector pin for corridors 1/2.
[00:35:27] Lina Gomez: RBAC gating and audit logs on the runbook.
[00:35:31] Elena Ruiz: communications draft due 10/07.
[00:35:34] Maya Chen: ok, next steps and owners on the sheet.
[00:35:38] [00:35:40] — brief cross-checking of calendar invites —
[00:36:02] Rajiv Menon: one more quick ask: for the regression endpoint, can we include a simple smoke signal that returns schema versioning so downstream parsers can assert compatibility?
[00:36:12] Samir Patel: yes, will add header X-RW-Schema: v1.2 in responses, and QA can assert.
[00:36:18] Rajiv Menon: thanks.
[00:36:21] Maya Chen: any blockers for owners to start their work today?
[00:36:26] Samir Patel: nothing blocking from eng side, but i need access to the canary spreadsheet. the link in chat works.
[00:36:31] Maya Chen: sent invite and edit perms.
[00:36:33] Elena Ruiz: i'll create the follow-up 30m sync for 10/08 and invite the oncall rotation.
[00:36:40] Maya Chen: great. last thing — quick risk tiering recap for the runbook preface: high (data-loss or security), medium (correctness/regression), low (perf/cost). we gate corridor transitions differently for each.
[00:36:55] Tom Hargreaves: sounds good.
[00:36:58] Maya Chen: ok, i'll close with explicit next steps in the sheet and PR the runbook.
[00:37:03] [00:37:04] — meeting wrap —
[00:37:06] Maya Chen: thanks everyone. recap will be in the doc and action items in firefly notes. if nothing else, see you on the 10/08 follow-up.
[00:37:14] Jules Park: thanks.
[00:37:16] Samir Patel: cheers.
[00:37:18] [00:37:19] — call ends —

Notes on transcription quality: multiple short overlaps and background noise; proper nouns sometimes garbled (kernel selector, KV-cache) — please verify names/links.
